Feeling in control of your money isn’t about doing more. It’s about having the right habits, quietly working in the background.

This monthly newsletter is your shortcut to simpler routines, fewer surprises, and more confidence in how your business is doing.

values.text: Look at profit, not just revenue
Most owners judge how they’re doing by their bank balance or sales. Neither tells you whether the business is working. For that, you need one thing: profit.

1. Revenue vs. profit
If sales are growing but profit isn’t, your costs are growing faster.

2. Your margin
Are you charging enough to cover what it costs to deliver?

3. Your pay
If you’re not paying yourself, the profit isn’t real yet.

Knowing your profit is the first step. Knowing your cash flow is the next.
A business can show a profit and still run out of cash.
PROFIT SHOWS HOW YOUR BUSINESS IS DOING
Why your bank balance can mislead you

You can be in profit and still be short of cash.

It comes down to timing: when money is earned vs. when it actually arrives.

Learn why they don’t match
Insurance helps you plan for the unexpected without upsetting your cash flow. Get covered in minutes.
Make your reports easier to read
Your list of accounts is the table of contents for your finances. Tidying it up makes it easier to see where money goes and to get useful reports.
Sol has run a martial arts school for 30 years. What’s kept it going isn’t just skill, it’s consistency: building a strong community and keeping a close eye on the numbers.
